No reason had been given, but he gathered unofficially from the Mayor of Chicago that the District complained of 'crowd-making and invasion of privacy.'

arxiv-2206-07638.title: Asynchronous SGD Beats Minibatch SGD Under Arbitrary Delays
arxiv-2206-07638.creator: Konstantin Mishchenko, Francis Bach, Mathieu Even, Blake Woodworth
arxiv-2206-07638.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Konstantin Mishchenko, Francis Bach, Mathieu Even, Blake Woodworth. The existing analysis of asynchronous stochastic gradient descent (SGD) degrades dramatically when any delay is large, giving the impression that performance depends primarily on the delay. On the contrary, we prove much better guarantees for the same asynchronous SGD algorithm regardless of the delays in the gradients, depending instead just on the number of parallel devices used to implement the algorithm.

arxiv-2207-03550.title: Trapped-particle microrheology of active suspensions
arxiv-2207-03550.creator: Zhiwei Peng, John F. Brady
arxiv-2207-03550.description: Abstract In microrheology, the local rheological properties such as viscoelasticity of a complex fluid are inferred from the free or forced motion of embedded colloidal probe particles. Theoretical machinery developed for forced-probe microrheology of colloidal suspensions focused on either constant-force (CF) or constant-velocity (CV) probes while in experiments neither the force nor the kinematics of the probe is fixed.

arxiv-2302-06023.title: Spin-selective strong light-matter coupling in a 2D hole gas-microcavity system
arxiv-2302-06023.creator: D. G. Suárez-Forero, D. W. Session, M. Jalali Mehrabad, P. Knüppel, S. Faelt, W. Wegscheider, M. Hafezi
arxiv-2302-06023.description: Abstract The interplay between time-reversal symmetry breaking and strong light-matter coupling in 2D gases brings intriguing aspects to polariton physics. This combination can lead to polarization/spin selective light-matter interaction in the strong coupling regime. In this work, we report such a selective strong light-matter interaction by harnessing a 2D gas in the quantum Hall regime coupled to a microcavity.

arxiv-2312-14360.title: Designing a skilled soccer team for RoboCup: exploring Skill-Set-Primitives through reinforcement learning
arxiv-2312-14360.creator: Miguel Abreu & Luis Paulo Reis, Nuno Lau
arxiv-2312-14360.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Miguel Abreu & Luis Paulo Reis, Nuno Lau. The RoboCup 3D Soccer Simulation League serves as a competitive platform for showcasing innovation in autonomous humanoid robot agents through simulated soccer matches. Our team, FC Portugal, developed a new codebase from scratch in Python after RoboCup 2021. The team’s performance relies on a set of skills centered around novel unifying primitives and a custom, symmetry-extended version of the Proximal Policy Optimization algorithm.

arxiv-2403-17360.title: Activity-Biometrics: Person Identification from Daily Activities
arxiv-2403-17360.creator: Shehreen Azad, Yogesh Singh Rawat
arxiv-2403-17360.description: Abstract In this work, we study a novel problem which focuses on person identification while performing daily activities. Learning biometric features from RGB videos is challenging due to spatio-temporal complexity and presence of appearance biases such as clothing color and background.

arxiv-2405-10312.title: KiDS-1000 and DES-Y1 combined: Cosmology from peak count statistics
arxiv-2405-10312.creator: Joachim Harnois-Déraps, Sven Heydenreich, Benjamin Giblin, Nicolas Martinet, Tilman Tröster, Marika Asgari, Pierre Burger, Tiago Castro, Klaus Dolag, Catherine Heymans, Hendrik Hildebrandt, Benjamin Joachimi & Angus H. Wright
arxiv-2405-10312.description: Abstract We analyse the fourth data release of the Kilo Degree Survey (KiDS-1000) and extract cosmological parameter constraints based on the cosmic shear peak count statistics. Peaks are identified in aperture mass maps in which the filter is maximally sensitive to angular scales in the range 2-4 arcmin , probing deep into the non-linear regime of structure formation.

arxiv-2408-06101.title: Generalization capabilities of MeshGraphNets to unseen geometries for fluid dynamics
arxiv-2408-06101.creator: Robin Schmöcker, Alexander Henkes, Julian Roth, Thomas Wick
arxiv-2408-06101.description: Abstract This works investigates the generalization capabilities of MeshGraphNets (MGN) [Pfaff et al. Learning Mesh-Based Simulation with Graph Networks. ICML 2021] to unseen geometries for fluid dynamics, e.g. predicting the flow around a new obstacle that was not part of the training data.

arxiv-2410-10556.title: Is Structure Dependence Shaped for Efficient Communication?: A Case Study on Coordination
arxiv-2410-10556.creator: Kohei Kajikawa, Yusuke Kubota, Yohei Oseki
arxiv-2410-10556.description: Abstract Natural language exhibits various universal properties. But why do these universals exist? One explanation is that they arise from functional pressures to achieve efficient communication , a view which attributes cross-linguistic properties to domain-general cognitive abilities. This hypothesis has successfully addressed some syntactic universal properties such as compositionality and Greenbergian word order universals.

arxiv-2502-10884.title: CodeA11y: Making AI Coding Assistants Useful for Accessible Web Development
arxiv-2502-10884.creator: Peya Mowar, Yi-Hao Peng, Jason Wu, Aaron Steinfeld, Jeffrey P. Bigham
arxiv-2502-10884.description: Abstract . A persistent challenge in accessible computing is ensuring developers produce web UI code that supports assistive technologies. Despite numerous specialized accessibility tools, novice developers often remain unaware of them, leading to ~96% of web pages that contain accessibility violations.

arxiv-2601-05569.title: Self-Evolving Distributed Memory Architecture for Scalable AI Systems
arxiv-2601-05569.creator: Zixuan Li 2 Chuanzhen Wang 1 Haotian Sun 3 1 Tongji University 2 Department of Artificial Intelligence, Pacific Coast University 3 Institute for Intelligent Systems, Northern Research Laboratory
arxiv-2601-05569.description: Abstract Distributed AI systems face critical memory management challenges across computation, communication, and deployment layers. RRAM-based in-memory computing suffers from scalability limitations due to device non-idealities and fixed array sizes. Decentralized AI frameworks struggle with memory efficiency across NAT-constrained networks due to static routing that ignores computational load.

pmc-11506349.creator: Rujuan Wu, Jiayi Yang, Qi Chen, Changxing Yang, Qianqian Ge, Danni Rui, Huazhong Xiang, Dawei Zhang, Cheng Wang, Xiaoqing Zhao
pmc-11506349.description: Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC) is the second most common malignant skin tumor. Early and precise diagnosis of tumor staging is crucial for long-term outcomes. While pathological diagnosis has traditionally served as the gold standard, the assessment of differentiation levels heavily depends on subjective judgments.

pmc-11664160.title: Protocol for single sensillum recording from labial olfactory sensory fields in spotted lanternfly
pmc-11664160.creator: Hany K.M. Dweck
pmc-11664160.description: SummaryMeasuring the electrophysiological responses of olfactory receptor neurons (ORNs) to odorants in spotted lanternfly (SLF) (Lycorma delicatula) is crucial for understanding how this invasive sap-feeding planthopper locates host plants, aggregates, and mates. Here, we present a protocol for single sensillum recording from SLF labial ORNs to measure their sensitivity, specificity, and response dynamics to odorants.

pmc-12731351.creator: Jiro Ichikawa, Kojiro Onohara, Tomohiro Inoue, Masanori Wako, Tetsuhiro Hagino, Kouhei Mitsui, Tomonori Kawasaki, Hirotaka Haro, Thomas Frauenfelder
pmc-12731351.description: We report a rare case of squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) arising from an intraosseous epidermal cyst (EC) in the distal phalanx of the left thumb. A 76-year-old male presented with progressive thumb pain experienced over the previous six months. Radiography revealed a radiolucent lesion without marginal sclerosis, and magnetic resonance imaging showed peripheral contrast enhancement with no solid components.

pmc-13507959.creator: N. Gopalakrishnan, B. Sridevi, R. Nalini Suja, M. Chitra, A. Subramani
pmc-13507959.description: Natural fiber-reinforced epoxy composites are increasingly popular as eco-friendly alternatives to synthetic materials due to their low density, biodegradability, and renewability. In this investigation, a unique hybrid epoxy biocomposite was produced using Aquilaria agallocha gum as a biofiller and snake grass and hemp fibers as reinforcement.

pmc-13562712.title: Multimodal fertility cues in chimpanzees: how body odours complement sexual swellings
pmc-13562712.creator: Marlen Kücklich, Madita Zetzsche, Sofya Dolotovskaya, Jakob W. Siepmann, Lydia Schmidt, Claudia Wiesner, Brigitte M. Weiß, Anja Widdig
pmc-13562712.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). To attract mating partners, female mammals communicate their reproductive status through one or multiple sensory modalities, providing redundant or complementary information. Chimpanzees (Pan troglodytes) are an excellent model for studying multimodal communication. Exaggerated sexual swellings of females serve as visual proxy for ovulation but their temporal imprecision suggests that olfactory cues may exist in addition to swellings to pinpoint fertility more accurately.
